##Load TPS
```{r}
#Read in the TPS data for all bee wing images

all_tps_data <- readland.tps("data/bee_wings.TPS",
                             specID = c("imageID"), readcurves = FALSE, 
                             warnmsg = TRUE,negNA = FALSE)

```

##Load csv Data
Read bee metadata to be merged with the TPS data.
```{r}
bee_data <- read_csv("data/bee_metadata.csv")

#df1 <- bee_data
#df1 <- df1 %>% separate(catalogNumber, c("UCSB", "number", "side")) #issue btwn _ vs - in catalogNumber
#bee_data_clean <- df1 %>% tidyr::unite('catalogNumber', sep = "_", c('UCSB','number', 'side')) #solving it by switching to _ from - in #the downloaded Hymenoptera data

bee_data_clean <- bee_data
```

### Generalized Procrustes Analaysis (GPA)
Run GPA on TPS data, to then generate coordinate data for each landmark on each specimen. In this code, we start with tps data and end with a CSV of coordinate data for each specimen. This can then be merged with the bee data generated above.
```{r}
all_tps_gpa <- gpagen(all_tps_data, PrinAxes = TRUE)

write.csv(all_tps_gpa$coords, "data/tpsGPA.csv", row.names = TRUE)

```

### Adjust the Landmark Data to usable format
```{r}
lmdata <- read.csv("data/tpsGPA.csv") #read landmark data in

df_transpose = t(lmdata) #transpose the landmark data
df_transpose1 <- df_transpose
df_transpose1 <- df_transpose1[-c(1),] #Remove first row
#Format of LM data is currently two rows per specimen
#with one row being X coordinate values and one row
#being Y coordinate values. Below, we split into two 
#data frames and then stitch them back together to get
#18 different variables for the 9 landmarks
#(9 X coordinates and 9 Y coordinates)
lm1 <- df_transpose1
lmX <- lm1
lmY <- lm1
lmX1 <- lmX
lmX1 <- data.frame(lmX1)
lmX2 <- setNames(cbind(rownames(lmX1), lmX1, row.names = NULL),
                 c("name", "LM1x", "LM2x", "LM3x",
                   "LM4x", "LM5x", "LM6x", "LM7x", "LM8x", "LM9x"))
lmXonly <- lmX2[str_detect(lmX2$name, "X."), ]
#repeat with Y
lmY1 <- lmY
lmY1 <- data.frame(lmY1)
lmY2 <- setNames(cbind(rownames(lmY1), lmY1, row.names = NULL),
                 c("name", "LM1y", "LM2y", "LM3y",
                   "LM4y", "LM5y", "LM6y", "LM7y", "LM8y", "LM9y"))
lmYonly <- lmY2[str_detect(lmY2$name, "Y."), ]
lmXonly1 <- lmXonly
lmYonly1 <- lmYonly
lmXonly2 <- lmXonly1 %>% 
    tidyr::separate(name,                      
                    c("X","collection", "barcode", "wing","species", 
                      "location", "wingSide"), extra='drop') %>%
    tidyr::unite('catalogNumber', c('collection', 'barcode', 'wing')) 
lmXonly3 <- lmXonly2[,c(2,6:14)]

##now: lmXonly5 has x coordinate values for all 9 landmarks, and just the catalogNumber
###repeat for Y
lmYonly2 <- lmYonly1 %>% 
    tidyr::separate(name,                      
                    c("Y","collection", "barcode", "wing","species", 
                      "location", "wingSide"), extra='drop') %>%
    tidyr::unite('catalogNumber', c('collection', 'barcode', "wing")) 
lmYonly3 <- lmYonly2[,c(2,6:14)]

#Now: unite the Y and X coordinate dataframes into just one
lm_both <- merge(lmXonly3, lmYonly3, by=("catalogNumber"))
```


### Merge Landmark and Curation Data
```{r}
lm_data <- merge(lm_both, bee_data_clean, by=c("catalogNumber"), all = FALSE)

lm_data %>% 
  distinct(catalogNumber, .keep_all = TRUE)

write.csv(lm_data, file = "data/LM_Data.csv")
```


### Create subset with equal numbers of specimens
Since there are different numbers of bee wings from each genus, we select the same number of bees from each genus to create a subset with equal number of wings.
```{r}
set.seed(339)  # for reproducibility so that the same subset is produced every time the code is run, if removed the code will produce a new randomly selected dataset

subset <- lm_data[!lm_data$Species %in% c("Andrena oenotherae", "Bombus vosnesenskii", "Ceratina punctagena", "Megachile rotundata"), ] # remove any extra species in dataset

subset2 <- unique(subset) # remove duplicates

ITD_data <- read.csv("data/ITD_covariates.csv")

subset3 <- merge(subset2, ITD_data, by=("catalogNumber"), all = TRUE) # merge land mark data with ITD data

subset_ITD <- subset3[!is.na(subset3$Species),]

# Include all specimens with ITD values and however many specimens without ITD values until a total subset of 10 specimens is reached
subset_LM <- subset_ITD %>% 
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    
    # Split into non-NA and NA
    non_na <- .x %>% filter(!is.na(ITD))
    na_rows <- .x %>% filter(is.na(ITD))
    
    if (nrow(non_na) >= 10) {
      # If ≥10 non-NA rows, randomly choose 10 of them
      slice_sample(non_na, n = 10)
      
    } else {
      # Otherwise, take all non-NA and fill with NA rows
      n_needed <- 10 - nrow(non_na)
      
      bind_rows(
        non_na,
        slice_sample(na_rows, n = min(n_needed, nrow(na_rows)))
      )
    }
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  relocate(Genus, .after = Species)

write.csv(subset_LM, file = "data/subset_LM.csv")
```

### MANOVA
Using MANOVA to test for difference between groups using the RRPP package.
```{r}
# MANOVA test between genera
manova_genus <- subset_LM #subset
manova_genus <- manova_genus[,c(2:23)] #drop catalog number and other non LM variables
manova_genus_data <- manova_genus[,c(1:18)] #drop genus variable
manova_genus_data <- as.matrix(manova_genus_data) #as matrix

fit_genus <- lm.rrpp(manova_genus_data ~ Genus, SS.type = "I", #Genus
               data = manova_genus, print.progress = FALSE) #run the linear model fit
fitm_genus <- manova.update(fit_genus, print.progress = FALSE, tol = 0) #run manova update

fit_subfam <- lm.rrpp(manova_genus_data ~ Subfamily, SS.type = "I", #Subfamily
               data = manova_genus, print.progress = FALSE) #run the linear model fit
fitm_subfam <- manova.update(fit_subfam, print.progress = FALSE, tol = 0) #run manova update

fit_fam <- lm.rrpp(manova_genus_data ~ Family, SS.type = "I", #Family
               data = manova_genus, print.progress = FALSE) #run the linear model fit
fitm_fam <- manova.update(fit_fam, print.progress = FALSE, tol = 0) #run manova update

# MANOVA Genus
summary(fitm_genus, test = "Pillai") #summarize with a manova table
capture.output(summary(fitm_genus, test = "Pillai"), file = "output/manova_pillai.txt")

# MANOVA Subfamily
summary(fitm_subfam, test = "Pillai") #summarize with a manova table
capture.output(summary(fitm_subfam, test = "Pillai"), file = "output/manova_pillai_subfam.txt")

# MANOVA Family
summary(fitm_fam, test = "Pillai") #summarize with a manova table
capture.output(summary(fitm_fam, test = "Pillai"), file = "output/manova_pillai_fam.txt")

```

### Load and Prune Phylogenetic Tree
```{r}
bee_tree <- ape::read.tree("data/BEE_mat7gen_p8pmAa_fst.nwk"); phytools::read.newick("data/BEE_mat7gen_p8pmAa_fst.nwk")

# Extract the genus from the tip labels
# Assuming the format is "genus_species~~family~~subfamily~tribe"
bee_tree$tip.label <- sub("_.*", "", bee_tree$tip.label)
bee_tree$tip.label <- sub("~.*", "", bee_tree$tip.label)
species_to_keep = c("Apis", "Bombus", "Agapostemon", "Xylocopa", "Osmia", "Megachile", "Diadasia", "Eucera", "Andrena", "Halictus", "Hesperapis", "Ceratina", "Habropoda", "Anthophora", "Panurginus", "Lasioglossum", "Calliopsis")

pruned_tree <- drop.tip(bee_tree, setdiff(bee_tree$tip.label, species_to_keep)) 
ref_tree <- pruned_tree

write.tree(ref_tree, file = "data/bee_tree.nwk")
write.nexus(ref_tree, file = "data/bee_tree.nex")
```

### Calculate Phylogenetic Distances
Extract the cophenetic (phylogenetic) distances from the phylogenetic tree.
```{r}
phylo_distances <- cophenetic.phylo(ref_tree)

write.csv(phylo_distances, "data/phylo_distances.csv", row.names = TRUE)
```

### Canonical Variate Analysis (CVA)
```{r}
vari <- subset_LM[,2:19]
species <- as.factor(subset_LM$Species)
genus <- as.factor(subset_LM$Genus)
subfamily <- as.factor(subset_LM$Subfamily)
family <- as.factor(subset_LM$Family)
catalog <- as.factor(subset_LM$catalogNumber)

cva.0 <- CVA(vari, groups = species, cv = TRUE) # canonical variate analysis @ species level
cva.1 <- CVA(vari, groups = genus, cv = TRUE) # canonical variate analysis @ generic level
cva.2 <- CVA(vari, groups = subfamily, cv = TRUE) # canonical variate analysis @ subfamily level
cva.3 <- CVA(vari, groups = family, cv = TRUE) # canonical variate analysis @ family level

# species
cva.0
# Variance explained by the canonical roots
cva.0$Var
# calculate the typicality probabilities and classification accuracy
typprobs_species <- typprobClass(cva.0$CVscores, groups = species)
print(typprobs_species)

# genus
cva.1
# Variance explained by the canonical roots
cva.1$Var
# calculate the typicality probabilities and classification accuracy
typprobs_genus <- typprobClass(cva.1$CVscores, groups = genus)
print(typprobs_genus)

# subfamily
cva.2
# Variance explained by the canonical roots
cva.2$Var
# calculate the typicality probabilities and classification accuracy
typprobs_subfamily <- typprobClass(cva.2$CVscores, groups = subfamily)
print(typprobs_subfamily)

# family
cva.3
# Variance explained by the canonical roots
cva.3$Var
# calculate the typicality probabilities and classification accuracy
typprobs_family <- typprobClass(cva.3$CVscores, groups = family)
print(typprobs_family)

```



### Visualize Canonical Variate Analysis - Genus

```{r}
# Extract CV scores into data frame
cva_df <- data.frame(
  CV1   = cva.1$CVscores[,1],
  CV2   = cva.1$CVscores[,2],
  Genus = factor(cva.1[["groups"]],
                 levels = sort(unique(cva.1[["groups"]]))), 
  Family = factor(cva.3[["groups"]],
                 levels = sort(unique(cva.3[["groups"]]))))
  

# centroid coordinates
centroids <- cva_df %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(
    CV1 = mean(CV1),
    CV2 = mean(CV2))

# Plot
ggplot(cva_df, aes(x = CV1, y = CV2)) +

  geom_point(aes(color = Genus,
                 shape = Genus),
             size = 2, stroke = 0.6) +

  # 95% confidence ellipses
  stat_ellipse(aes(color = Genus),
               level = 0.95, show.legend = FALSE) +
  
  # group means (centroids)
  geom_point(data = centroids,
             aes(x = CV1, y = CV2, color = Genus),
             shape = 16,
             size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  
   # Point shapes
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(1:17)) +
  
  # axis labels with explained variance
  labs(
    x = paste("1st canonical axis",
              round(cva.1$Var[1,2], 1), "%"),
    
    y = paste("2nd canonical axis",
              round(cva.1$Var[2,2], 1), "%"),
    
    color = "Genus",
    shape = "Genus") +
  
  theme_light() + 
  
  theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 10), legend.text  = element_text(size = 10))

ggsave("output/CVA_genus.png", plot = last_plot(), dpi = 300, width = 10, height = 5, units = "in")
```
### Visualize Canonical Variate Analysis - Genus (Colored by Family)
```{r}

cva_df <- data.frame(
  CV1   = cva.1$CVscores[,1],
  CV2   = cva.1$CVscores[,2],
  Genus = factor(cva.1[["groups"]],
                 levels = sort(unique(cva.1[["groups"]]))),
  Family = factor(cva.3[["groups"]],
                  levels = sort(unique(cva.3[["groups"]]))))

# centroid coordinates
centroids <- cva_df %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(CV1 = mean(CV1), CV2 = mean(CV2))

# Genus by Family
genus_family <- cva_df %>%
  distinct(Genus, Family) %>%
  arrange(Family, Genus)          # sorted by family, then genus

# legend order: genera grouped by family
genus_order <- as.character(genus_family$Genus)

# family color
family_cols <- c("Andrenidae"  = "indianred3",
                 "Apidae"      = "#E5BB53",
                 "Halictidae"  = "seagreen3",
                 "Megachilidae"= "steelblue2",
                 "Melittidae"  = "mediumorchid2")
  
# genus = family color
genus_cols <- setNames(
  family_cols[as.character(genus_family$Family)],
  genus_order)

# one shape per genus
genus_shapes <- setNames(
  rep_len(1:17, length(genus_order)),
  genus_order)

# Plot
ggplot(cva_df, aes(x = CV1, y = CV2)) +

  geom_point(aes(color = Genus, shape = Genus),
             size = 2, stroke = 0.6) +

  # 95% confidence ellipses
  stat_ellipse(aes(color = Genus, group = Genus),
               level = 0.95, show.legend = FALSE) +

  # group means (centroids)
  geom_point(data = centroids,
             aes(x = CV1, y = CV2, color = Genus),
             shape = 16, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +

  # breaks controls legend order; both scales must match to stay merged
  scale_color_manual(values = genus_cols, breaks = genus_order) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = genus_shapes, breaks = genus_order) +

  labs(
    x = paste("1st canonical axis", round(cva.1$Var[1,2], 1), "%"),
    y = paste("2nd canonical axis", round(cva.1$Var[2,2], 1), "%"),
    color = "Genus",
    shape = "Genus") +

  theme_light() +
  theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.text  = element_text(size = 10))

ggsave("output/CVA_genus2.png", plot = last_plot(), dpi = 300, width = 10, height = 5, units = "in")

```

### Calculate Phylogenetic Signal
Calculate phylogenetic signal (Multivariate K and Lambda) from Procrustes shape variables, using effect size estimated from likelihood.
```{r}

LMmeans <- cva.1$groupmeans #mean landmark values per genus

#Test for phylogenetic signal across all landmarks
physig_LMs_K <- physignal(A = LMmeans, phy = ref_tree, iter = 999) #Multivariate Blomberg's K
summary(physig_LMs_K)

physig_LMs <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans, phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean", iter = 999) #Phylogenetic signal effect size (Z)
summary(physig_LMs)



#Test for phylogenetic signal effect size for each individual landmark (include both x and y coordinate)
physig_LM1 <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans[,c("LM1x", "LM1y")], phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean") #Landmark 1
summary(physig_LM1)

physig_LM2 <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans[,c("LM2x", "LM2y")], phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean") #Landmark 2
summary(physig_LM2)

physig_LM3 <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans[,c("LM3x", "LM3y")], phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean") #Landmark 3
summary(physig_LM3)

physig_LM4 <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans[,c("LM4x", "LM4y")], phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean") #Landmark 4
summary(physig_LM4)

physig_LM5 <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans[,c("LM5x", "LM5y")], phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean") #Landmark 5
summary(physig_LM5)

physig_LM6 <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans[,c("LM6x", "LM6y")], phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean") #Landmark 6
summary(physig_LM6)

physig_LM7 <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans[,c("LM7x", "LM7y")], phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean") #Landmark 7
summary(physig_LM7)

physig_LM8 <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans[,c("LM8x", "LM8y")], phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean") #Landmark 8
summary(physig_LM8)

physig_LM9 <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans[,c("LM9x", "LM9y")], phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean") #Landmark 9
summary(physig_LM9)

physig_LM3 <- physignal.z(A = LMmeans[,c("LM3x", "LM3y")], phy = ref_tree, lambda = "mean") #Landmark 3
summary(physig_LM3)


#Compare phylogenetic effect sizes between landmarks
physig_compare <- compare.physignal.z(physig_LM1, physig_LM2, physig_LM3, physig_LM4, physig_LM5, physig_LM6, physig_LM7, physig_LM8, physig_LM9)
summary(physig_compare)
```

### Phylogenetic Tree Reconstruction
Estimate phylogeny from mahalanobis distance matrix produced by CVA by Neighbor-Joining
```{r}
MahaMatrix <- cva.1[["Dist"]][["GroupdistMaha"]] #mahalanobis distance matrix

# Build a Neighbor-Joining tree (unrooted by default)
nj_tree <- nj(MahaMatrix)
ggtree(nj_tree,branch.length="branch.length", cex = 0.75) + geom_tiplab(size = 2) 
write.tree(nj_tree, file = "data/nj_tree.nwk")

```

### Calculate Phylogenetic Tree Similarity by Quartet
```{r}
#Reference Tree vs Neigchbor-Joining Tree
RefvsNJ <- QuartetStatus(ref_tree, nj_tree)
SimilarityMetrics(RefvsNJ, similarity = TRUE)[,"SimilarityToReference"]

VisualizeQuartets(ref_tree, nj_tree)
plot(cophylo(ref_tree, nj_tree, rotate = TRUE), link.type = "curved", link.lwd = 2, link.col = make.transparent("red", 0.5))

#Calculate p-value
obs <- SimilarityMetrics(RefvsNJ)[,"ExplicitlyAgree"]
taxa <- ref_tree$tip.label

nperm <- 1000

perm_stats <- numeric(nperm)

for(i in 1:nperm){

 # random tree topology
  rand_tree <- rtree(17, rooted = TRUE, tip.label = taxa, br = runif, equiprob = FALSE)

  # compare to observed tree
  qs_perm <- QuartetStatus(ref_tree, rand_tree)

  perm_stats[i] <- SimilarityMetrics(qs_perm)[,"ExplicitlyAgree"]
}

pval_nj <- (sum(perm_stats >= obs) + 1) / (nperm + 1)

pval_nj

hist(perm_stats,  xlim = c(min(perm_stats), 0.75), xlab = "Quartet Similarity", main = NA)
abline(v = obs, col = 2, lwd = 5)
```

### Allometric Linear Regression
```{r}
set.seed(339)  # for reproducibility so that the same subset is produced every time the code is run, if removed the code will produce a new randomly selected dataset

metadata <- subset_LM[,-c(2:19)]

CVscores <- cva.1$CVscores

CV_ITD_data <- cbind(CVscores, metadata)
write.csv(CV_ITD_data, "data/CV_ITD_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)

CV_sub <- CV_ITD_data[!is.na(CV_ITD_data$ITD), ]

CV_sub <- CV_sub %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  slice_sample(n = 5) %>%
  ungroup()

# Plot colors (Genera colored by Family)
family_cols <- c("Andrenidae"   = "indianred3",
                 "Apidae"       = "#E5BB53",
                 "Halictidae"   = "seagreen3",
                 "Megachilidae" = "steelblue2",
                 "Melittidae"   = "mediumorchid2")

genus_family <- CV_sub %>%
  distinct(Genus, Family) %>%
  arrange(Family, Genus)

genus_order <- as.character(genus_family$Genus)

genus_cols <- setNames(
  family_cols[as.character(genus_family$Family)],
  genus_order)

genus_shapes <- setNames(
  rep_len(1:17, length(genus_order)),
  genus_order)

# Plot
ggplot(data = CV_sub, aes(x = ITD, y = `CV 1`)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = factor(Genus),
                 shape = factor(Genus)),
             size = 2, stroke = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = genus_cols, breaks = genus_order) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = genus_shapes, breaks = genus_order) +
  labs(x = "ITD (cm)", y = "Canonical Variate 1 (CV1)", color = "Genus", shape = "Genus") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  theme_light()

# Regression Statistics
ITD_regession <- lm(formula = `CV 1` ~ `ITD`, data = CV_sub) #Linear Regression Model 'y ~ x'
summary(ITD_regession)

ggsave("output/allo_regression.png", plot = last_plot(), dpi = 600, width = 10, height = 5, units = "in")

```

### Phylogenetic Generalised Least Squares (PGLS) Analysis 
Procrustes ANOVA in a phylogenetic framework and uses permutation procedures to assess statistical hypotheses describing patterns of shape variation and covariation for a set of Procrustes-aligned coordinates
```{r}
subset_ITD <- subset_LM[!is.na(subset_LM$ITD), ]

subset_ITD$ITD <- as.numeric(subset_ITD$ITD)

mean_ITD <-  aggregate(ITD ~ Genus, data = subset_ITD, FUN = mean) %>% 
  column_to_rownames(var = "Genus")

mean_ITD$ITD <- as.numeric(mean_ITD$ITD)

ITD_pgls <- geomorph.data.frame(
  shape = LMmeans,
  size  = mean_ITD,
  phy   = ref_tree)

taxa <- rownames(LMmeans)
cols <- scales::hue_pal()(17)
shapes <- c(1:17)

### Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) Linear Regression
# Shape ~ size (allometry)
fit_ols <- procD.lm(shape ~ size.ITD, data = ITD_pgls, iter = 9999)
summary(fit_ols)

# Predline
par(mar=c(5, 5, 3, 8), xpd=TRUE)
plotAllometry(fit_ols, size = ITD_pgls$size.ITD, logsz = FALSE, 
method = "PredLine", pch = shapes, col = cols)
legend("topright", legend = taxa, col = cols, pch = shapes, 
       cex = 0.85, ncol = 1, x = "right", inset = c(-0.26,0), xpd=TRUE, bty = "n")

# RegScore
par(mar=c(5, 5, 3, 8), xpd=TRUE)
plotAllometry(fit_ols, size = ITD_pgls$size.ITD, logsz = FALSE, 
method = "RegScore", cex = 1.2, pch = shapes, col = cols, xlab = "ITD (cm)")
legend("topright", legend = taxa, col = cols, pch = shapes, 
       cex = 0.85, ncol = 1, x = "right", inset = c(-0.26,0), xpd=TRUE, bty = "n")

# CAC
plotAllometry(fit_ols, size = ITD_pgls$size.ITD, logsz = TRUE, 
method = "CAC", col = cols, pch = shapes)


### Phylogenetic Generalised Least Squares (PGLS) Linear Regression
# Shape ~ size (allometry), accounting for phylogeny
fit_pgls <- procD.pgls(shape ~ size.ITD, phy = ref_tree, data = ITD_pgls, lambda = 0.2143, iter = 9999) #lambda = 0.2143 from physignal.z() results
summary(fit_pgls)

# Predline
par(mar=c(5, 5, 3, 8), xpd=TRUE)
plotAllometry(fit_pgls, size = ITD_pgls$size.ITD, logsz = FALSE, 
method = "PredLine", col = cols, pch = shapes)
legend("topright", legend = taxa, col = cols, pch = shapes, 
       cex = 0.85, ncol = 1, x = "right", inset = c(-0.26,0), xpd=TRUE, bty = "n")

# RegScore
par(mar=c(5, 5, 3, 8), xpd=FALSE)

plotAllometry(fit_pgls, size = ITD_pgls$size.ITD, logsz = FALSE, 
              method = "RegScore", cex = 1.2, pch = shapes, col = cols, xlab = "ITD (cm)", ylab = "Wing Shape")

legend(legend = taxa, col = cols, pch = shapes, 
       cex = 0.85, ncol = 1, x = "right", inset = c(-0.26,0), xpd = NA, bty = "n")

# CAC
plotAllometry(fit_pgls, size = ITD_pgls$size.ITD, logsz = TRUE, 
method = "CAC", col = cols, pch = shapes)


?procD.pgls
```
